question: Air travel is a very important mode of intra-EU transport, and is increasingly being used by the elderly, people with disabilities and pregnant women. Flight cancellations and delays can be particularly burdensome for these vulnerable groups.

Providing them with access to certain support services – such as free accommodation in airport hotels for wait times exceeding four hours, on-site nursing care, reimbursement of unforeseen medical expenses and baggage assistance – might reduce the inconvenience caused.

Other measures could also significantly improve these passengers’ travel experience, such as reimbursing the cost of buying essential and useful items and granting them priority access to check-in, security and boarding lanes.

In the light of the above, is the Commission planning to strengthen social care policies for vulnerable passengers affected by flight disruptions, with a view to greater passenger protection and inclusion on flights within the EU?
answer: The EU legislation on the rights of passengers travelling by air establishes a minimum level of care for all passengers if their flight is cancelled or whenever a delay reaches a certain time limit beyond the scheduled time of departure (1). This care is linked to the waiting time resulting from the long delay or cancellation and subsequent re-routing.

The care should include some or all of the following elements of assistance, depending on the circumstances of each specific case: provision of meals and refreshments, accommodation and transport to the accommodation and return to the airport and two telephone calls, telex, fax messages or e-mails. The care shall be proportionate, reasonable, and adapted to the circumstances of the disruption.

This legislation already takes into consideration the special needs of certain vulnerable passengers by stipulating that operating air carriers shall pay particular attention to the needs of persons with reduced mobility and any persons accompanying them, as well as to the needs of unaccompanied children (2) and ensure that assistance is provided as soon as possible (3).
The Commission has also published interpretative guidelines (4) on how this rule should be implemented in practice (5).

In addition, the Commission proposed by means of its recent legislative proposal on passenger rights in a multimodal context (6), to extend the obligation of operating carriers to pay particular attention to the needs of persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility, the persons accompanying them and their assistance dogs if such passengers miss the connection of a subsequent transport service during a multimodal journey concluded under a single multimodal contract.

See Article 9 of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 February 2004 establishing common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights, and repealing Regulation (EEC) No 295/OJ L 46, 17.2.2004, p. 1. See Article 9(3) of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004.

Commission Notice — Interpretative Guidelines on Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long delay of flights and on Council Regulation (EC) No 2027/97 on air carrier liability in the event of accidents as amended by Regulation (EC) No 889/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council (2016/C 214/04).

Operating air carriers should also ensure, where available, that accommodation is accessible for people with disabilities and their service dogs. See Article 9(2) of the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on passenger rights in the context of multimodal journeys COM(2023) 752 final.
